minutes.headline: Board deemed a Flat Hill Road dog dangerous and ordered restraint; it signaled no solar pilot without a PPA.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with a sworn hearing on a dangerous dog complaint over a July 5 incident; the board found the dog dangerous on a split vote and ordered humane restraint and muzzling off the property. It approved a fuel-efficient vehicle policy for the Green Communities application and heard Nugen's request for a solar pilot agreement for the West Street site, which members said they could not support without a power purchase agreement. It also discussed quorum and open meeting law enforcement and heard committee reports.

what_happened.line: The board found a Flat Hill Road dog dangerous on a split vote after a sworn hearing on a July incident.
It then ordered humane restraint and muzzling off the premises, with one no vote heard; an order will go out by certified mail with a 10 day appeal period.
The board approved a fuel-efficient vehicle policy, part of the Green Communities application.
The board indicated it would not support a West Street solar pilot agreement without a matching power purchase agreement, and may revisit it later.
The school building committee reported the project estimate came in just under the target range, with the state reimbursement rate lower in practice than stated.

why_it_matters: The solar pilot agreement sets what a developer pays the town in place of ordinary property tax on equipment for 20 years, so the board's position affects future town revenue.
The school building estimate and the reimbursement rate feed the borrowing and tax impact that residents will likely be asked to vote on.
The dog order shows how a dangerous-dog finding turns into enforceable conditions for the owner, with a set appeal window.
